the PTMEs were found at concentrations of 0.2–1.0 ng/g dry sediment, with miliacin being most abundant (0.4–1.0), while the esters were found at concentrations ranging from 0.5 to 3 ng/g dry sediment.
PTMEs and triterpenol acetates and hexanates are useful for tracking the fate of terrestrial organic detritus in aquatic systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PTMEs and triterpenol acetates and hexanotes are good biomarkers for assessing the sources and diagenesis of organic matter in aquatic environments.
PTMEs can be used as biomarkers of specific subspecies of plants in the Cross-River region.
PTMEs are not just a product of diagenetic alteration, but also a primary constituent of higher plants, especially in the Cross-River basin.
